newsitem.title: USA: AT&T posts expected decline in operating income.
newsitem.headline: AT&T posts expected decline in operating income.

text.p: AT&T Corp. reported an expected decline in third quarter operating earnings Wednesday while most regional Bell companies posted robust gains.
AT&T, which had announced last month that it expected its earnings to fall short of year-ago results and Wall Street's expectations, said its income from continuing operations fell 11 percent.
Meanwhile, local phone companies BellSouth Corp., Bell Atlantic Corp., SBC Communications Inc. and Pacific Telesis all reported stronger earnings.

AT&T reported net income of $1.43 billion, or 89 cents a share, up from $262 million, or 16 cents a share, in the year-ago period when it took a one-time charge of $1.6 billion for its restructuring and for cost reductions at its NCR computer unit, which it hopes to spin off by year-end.

The company had projected last month that its income from continuing operations would be lower in the third quarter. Operating earnings fell to $1.36 billion, or 84 cents a share, from $1.53 billion, or 96 cents a share.
AT&T said on Sept. 24 that operating income was hurt by competitive pressure in the long-distance telephone market, customer service costs and investments in local, online and wireless capacity.
Sales at the nation's largest long-distance carrier rose to $13.2 billion from $12.9 billion.
AT&T's stock fell 12.5 cents to $39.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.

AT&T's earnings were in line with analysts' estimates, which were revised after September's profit warning, but few gave hope for a quick rebound now that AT&'s fortunes are so closely tied to the long-distance marketplace.
The regional bells, on the other hand, show no sign of slowing their growth rates, analysts said.
"I would characterise the quarter as a cause for celebration in just about every instance," said Bill Vogel of Dillon Read, a long-time bull on regional Bell stocks.
BellSouth Corp., which provides local telephone services in the Southeast, reported record operating income and sales for the quarter.
Net income rose 12.9 percent to $631 million and revenues were up 9 percent at $4.83 billion.
Atlanta-based BellSouth also said it added 222,000 new telephone lines, a record for the third quarter.
"This is the highest profit from operations for any quarter in the company's history," said Chairman John Clendenin.
Philadelphia-based Bell Atlantic Corp., which provides local telephone service in the mid-Atlantic states, said profit rose 9.4 percent and its sales grew 7.6 percent.

Bell Atlantic said it earned $483 million, or $1.10 a share, compared with $441.9 million, or $1.01 a share. The year-ago results excluded a one-time gain of about $203 million from the sale of cellular properties and charges of about $40 million associated with some business development ventures and contracts.
Revenues rose to $3.30 billion from $3.26 billion.
SBC Communications Inc., the San Antonio, Texas-based parent of local telephone company Southwestern Bell, said it earned a record $593 million on record sales of $3.6 billion in the third quarter.
Revenue from telephone operations grew 8.5 percent. Over the last 12 months, residential access lines increased 3.7 percent and business lines grew 8.4 percent.

The earnings amounted to 97 cents a share, which compared with a year-ago loss of $2.82 billion, or $3.75 a share, on revenue of $3.29 billion. The year-ago loss came after an extraordinary $2.8 billion charge for accounting changes.
Pacific Telesis, local telephone service provider in California and Nevada, said it earned $286 million, or 67 cents a share, on revenue of $2.42 billion.

A year earlier, San Francisco-based PacTel lost $3.09 billion, or $7.22 a share, on sales of $2.28 billion. The year-earlier period included a one-time charge of $3.36 billion, or $7.86 a share, for accounting changes.
